content.text: {"label":"marketing_campaign","explanation":"Payments volume began rising in the 11:00 interval and climbed to 52% above forecast at 11:30 (SL fell to 32%, 27 abandons). The timing follows the 10:55 'Reward points expiring - redeem now' email to 500,000 card holders. The excess is in other_payments (1.77x), refund_status (1.56x) and card_declined (1.33x). AHT is on forecast and payments staffing matches plan, so this is extra demand, not lost capacity. There is no customer-facing incident: the only open one is a P4 on the HR portal. upi_payment_failed is below normal, which also argues against a payments outage. Payments attendance is normal (0 absences logged). General shows only mild extra volume (+9%). Its 11:30 SL dip (19%) came with a one-interval AHT spike (406 s vs 335 s forecast), which looks like noise rather than a new trend.","plan_name":"Payments campaign surge: absorb the peak and add capacity through mid-afternoon","rationale":"Campaign surges usually peak within a few hours of the send and then decay, so the plan concentrates capacity on payments from 12:00 to about 16:15. Delaying breaks is free and covers the next hour or so. Cancelling payments coaching returns agents to the phones at low cost. Two consecutive overtime offers cover the gap until 16:15: overtime agents arrive 30 minutes after approval, so they start at 12:15. Expected acceptance is about 6 and 4 agents, roughly Rs 7,200 in total, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget. Callback smooths the queue peaks by moving work to quieter periods later in the day. Chat deflection of refund_status and payment_status_enquiry calls (both allowed reasons, and refund_status is rising) removes some calls at Rs 12 per chat. No cross-skilled move from general, because general fell to 19% SL at 11:30 and cannot reliably stay above 70%. General gets a short, free break delay to steady it after the AHT spike.
